argument_summary: Certification is supportable only as a documentation-conditioned outcome, not as a clean no-issue approval. The admissible record shows the current release clears aggregate readiness and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, but it also shows a current material subgroup weakness in the health-plan benefits support slice. Under the stated policy, the defensible position is to treat certification as acceptable only if the current release documentation expressly reflects that limitation or an approved mitigation covers it. Prior approval and informal monitoring context narrow the concern but do not eliminate the current documentation requirement.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is limiting, not permissive: certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation. On the present record, prior approval from nine weeks ago and the release-thread monitoring comment are contextual evidence only; they do not substitute for current evidence, reviewed mitigation, or approved risk acceptance. The strongest supportable policy reading is therefore caveated compliance tied to explicit current-release documentation of the subgroup regression.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is needed to justify the position. The supportable case rests on the admissible governance record alone. Any remaining uncertainty can be handled through bounded certification caveats rather than escalation, provided the packet is framed as documentation-conditioned compliance.
concessions: The current health-plan benefits support slice is below the warning threshold and is a real limitation, not a resolved issue.
The prior approved release does not establish compliance for this release because the corpus and evaluation set changed.
The record does not contain reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or attached disclosure language, so clean certification is not supportable.
